decision: Wire The Admin's Claude Code hooks into the repo-root .claude/settings.json, with each hook script checking file_path for a school-admissions-assistant/ prefix before applying its rule, rather than giving school-admissions-assistant/ its own git repo.
rationale: Claude Code's hook/settings discovery is scoped to the git repository root, not arbitrary subdirectories. school-admissions-assistant/ has no .git of its own, and direct testing (a debug hook dumping raw PreToolUse/PostToolUse payloads) confirmed its nested settings.json was never read. Root-wiring with path-scoped script logic is the minimal fix that makes hooks actually fire without restructuring how the project is developed or committed.
alternatives_considered: Split school-admissions-assistant/ into its own git repository so its own settings.json becomes authoritative — rejected: bigger, more disruptive structural change (separate history/remote) than the task called for, and breaks the single-repo workflow used throughout Modules 10-12.
Leave the nested settings.json as documentation only and accept the hooks are inert — rejected: defeats the entire point of Part B, which requires a hook that actually blocks a real action.
